title: Meta Muse AI Agent Launches in UK with Purchase Controls
summary: Meta's Muse AI agent officially launched in the UK on November 23, 2026. Every purchase requires explicit user approval via secure credentials store.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Meta officially launched Muse AI agent for UK adults on November 23, 2026, marking the first Big Tech AI agent product shipped in the UK market.
- Muse autonomously executes tasks across partner apps like Marks & Spencer, Ocado, and Trainline, but requires explicit user approval for every purchase via secure credentials store.
- Meta acknowledged prompt injection remains an open problem and uses isolated runtime with Sentinel permission authority to limit potential security damage from agent actions.


Meta officially launched Muse, its personal AI agent, for UK adults on November 23, 2026, becoming the first Big Tech company to ship an AI agent product in the United Kingdom. The autonomous assistant handles tasks like booking travel, managing refunds, and coordinating shopping across integrated apps, but every purchase requires explicit user approval before execution.


## Partner Ecosystem and Core Capabilities


Muse integrates with launch partners including Marks & Spencer, Ocado, Trainline, Currys, easyJet, Spotify, and OpenTable. The agent autonomously plans and executes multi-step workflows across these services, handling tasks from comparing insurance quotes to tracking school calendars. Users connect the apps they want Muse to access, with granular permission controls determining whether the agent can read, send, or execute actions within each service.


The system can proactively review connected email accounts to surface important messages, convert saved Instagram Reels into shopping lists, and coordinate logistics across multiple platforms. Meta automatically connects Facebook, Instagram, and Threads accounts when users sign up through an existing Meta account in the same Accounts Center.


## Security Architecture and Permission Model


Meta implemented a layered security model with an isolated runtime environment and Sentinel permission authority that validates every action against granted permissions. User credentials including passwords and usernames are stored in a secure credentials store that allows Muse to complete authorized actions without exposing sensitive data to the underlying AI model. The system automatically ignores one-time codes and password-reset links in email to prevent credential leakage.


Users control approval frequency through settings, choosing between per-action confirmation or longer-duration permissions for specific task types. All purchases mandate individual approval regardless of other permission settings. Meta maintains a complete audit log of every action Muse has executed and plans to take, allowing users to review the agent's activity history at any point.


## Prompt Injection Acknowledgment


Meta explicitly acknowledged that prompt injection, a vulnerability where malicious instructions embedded in external content can hijack agent behavior, "remains an open problem" across the AI industry. The company relies on runtime isolation and the Sentinel permission layer to contain potential damage from compromised instructions, but did not claim to have solved the fundamental security challenge.


The UK's Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum issued a warning that AI agents "may amplify and accelerate risks" to consumers, highlighting regulatory scrutiny of autonomous systems with purchasing authority. Meta stated it has engaged constructively with appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue ongoing collaboration.


## Privacy Controls and Data Usage


Conversations with Muse and stored personal information remain separate from Meta's advertising systems. Users can opt out of having their interactions used to develop and improve Meta's AI models, though this setting defaults to enabled at signup. When training data is collected, Meta removes identifying details like names, email addresses, and phone numbers. Private messages from email or Instagram Direct Messages are excluded from model training entirely.


The system stores memory of user preferences to eliminate repetitive instructions, with full user access to view, edit, or delete remembered information. A complete reset option allows users to wipe all Muse data and restart from scratch.


## Availability and Rollout Timeline


Officially launched on November 23, 2026, Muse is available to all UK adults through new account creation or by connecting an existing Meta account. The UK launch represents Meta's first international market for the agent product, positioning the company ahead of competing Big Tech AI agent offerings in the region.


## What This Means


Meta's UK launch of Muse establishes a new standard for AI agent deployment that balances autonomy with explicit user control, particularly around financial transactions. The mandatory purchase approval model and transparent acknowledgment of unsolved security challenges like prompt injection set precedent for how tech companies navigate regulatory environments skeptical of autonomous AI systems. The extensive partner ecosystem demonstrates commercial readiness for AI agents that operate across fragmented service landscapes, though the security architecture suggests Meta views containment rather than prevention as the realistic near-term approach to agent safety risks.
